# Hamropedia.com

A hand-built, static website: free Nepali tools, a free AI & machine learning roadmap,
study-abroad guides for Nepali students, and sourced Nepal news. It replaces the old
WordPress site and keeps every old article URL working.

**Stack:** plain HTML/CSS/JS generated by a ~200-line Node build script (`build.mjs`).
Dependencies: `marked`, `gray-matter`, `highlight.js` (and `sharp` for images, dev only).
Hosted free on GitHub Pages.

## What's on the site

| Section | URL | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Home | `/` | `src/pages/home.js` |
| Blog, categories | `/blog/`, `/category/<slug>/` | `src/pages/posts.js` |
| News | `/news/` | posts with `type: news` |
| Articles | `/<slug>/` (same URLs as WordPress) | `src/content/posts/*.md` |
| AI & ML Roadmap | `/ai-roadmap/`, `/ai-roadmap/<phase>/` | `src/data/roadmap.json` (resources from AtomicHub) |
| English → Nepali typing | `/tools/english-to-nepali/` | `src/assets/js/lib/romanized.js` |
| Preeti ↔ Unicode | `/tools/preeti-to-unicode/` | `src/assets/js/lib/preeti.js` |
| Nepali date converter | `/tools/nepali-date-converter/` | `src/assets/js/lib/bs-date.js` |
| About, contact, privacy, terms | old WordPress URLs | `src/pages/static.js` |

Also generated: `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt`, `rss.xml`, `404.html`, redirect pages for
retired posts (`redirects` in `src/data/site.js`), Open Graph images, JSON-LD structured data.

## Run it locally

```bash
npm install
npm test          # converter tests (Preeti vectors, typing rules, every BS date)
npm run dev       # build + serve at http://localhost:4321
npm run verify    # check links, images, old URLs, titles, descriptions
```

## Write a new post

1. Create `src/content/posts/my-new-post.md` (the file name becomes the URL `/my-new-post/`):

   ```markdown
   ---
   title: "The title people see"
   seoTitle: "Optional: a longer title for Google"
   description: "One or two sentences (about 150 characters) for Google and social cards."
   date: 2026-11-15
   updated: 2026-11-20        # optional, show when you change it later
   category: nepal            # study-abroad | coding | ai | nepal
   type: news                 # optional: news shows it on /news/
   tags: [nepal, economy]
   coverWord: "Budget"        # 1-2 words drawn on the card artwork
   coverAlt: "Describe the cover for screen readers"
   ---

   Your article in Markdown. Use ## for sections (they become the table of contents).

   > **Update:** blockquotes starting with **Update:**, **Note:**, **Tip:** or
   > **Important:** become coloured callout boxes.
   ```

2. Put screenshots in `public/images/posts/<folder>/` (run
   `node scripts/optimize-images.mjs public/images/posts/<folder> path/to/*.png` to resize
   and convert them to WebP) and use `![alt text](/images/posts/<folder>/x.webp "caption")`.
3. `npm run covers` makes the card artwork and social image for the new post.
4. Commit and push to `main`. GitHub Actions tests, builds, verifies and deploys.

**House rules for content:** link a source for every fact, number and fee; label
proposals as proposals; show the updated date when you change something.

## Deploying (GitHub Pages + your Hostinger domain)

Do these **in this order**. Setting the custom domain on GitHub *before* changing DNS
stops anyone else from claiming the domain on GitHub in between.

1. Push this folder to a **public** GitHub repository (free GitHub Pages needs a public
   repo). In **Settings → Pages** set **Source: GitHub Actions**, wait for the first
   deploy to go green, then set **Custom domain** to `hamropedia.com`.
   (The temporary `username.github.io/repo/` address will look broken: the site is built
   for the root of its own domain. That's expected.)
2. In **Hostinger → Domains → DNS / Nameservers → DNS records**:
   - delete the existing `A` **and `AAAA`** records for `@` that point to Hostinger hosting
     (a leftover `AAAA` record would keep sending some visitors to WordPress);
   - add four `A` records for `@`: `185.199.108.153`, `185.199.109.153`,
     `185.199.110.153`, `185.199.111.153`;
   - optional IPv6: four `AAAA` records for `@`: `2606:50c0:8000::153`,
     `2606:50c0:8001::153`, `2606:50c0:8002::153`, `2606:50c0:8003::153`;
   - replace whatever `www` record exists with a `CNAME` to `<your-github-username>.github.io`;
   - **keep all `MX`, `TXT` (including SPF and `google-site-verification`) and email records.**
     Search Console verification for this domain is not in the WordPress HTML, so it is
     probably a DNS `TXT` record: deleting it would un-verify the site.
3. Wait for DNS (minutes to a few hours), then tick **Enforce HTTPS** in Settings → Pages.
4. In [Google Search Console](https://search.google.com/search-console), submit
   `https://hamropedia.com/sitemap.xml`. (`/sitemap_index.xml`, the old WordPress
   sitemap address, also still works.) Use **URL inspection → Request indexing** for the
   home page and the tools. Keep the WordPress hosting until the new site is live and
   checked, then cancel it.

`public/ads.txt` keeps the AdSense publisher line from the old site. The new site shows
no ads; if you add AdSense later, update the privacy policy (cookies) first.

## Keeping things fresh

- `npm run check-links` checks every roadmap resource link; `npm run check-post-links`
  checks article links (some sites block bots with 403, which is usually fine).
- The Nepali calendar table is confirmed for 2000–2083 BS; update `MONTH_DAYS` in
  `bs-date.js` when the official 2084+ calendar is published, and move `BS_PROVISIONAL_FROM`.
- `_wp-export/` (git-ignored) holds the WordPress export and a full backup of the old
  uploads. Never commit it: it contains email addresses from the old site.
